policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 59:10 reads 'My God with his lovingkindness will meet me': the third-person suffix 'his lovingkindness' renders the ketiv חסדו, not the qere חַסְדִּי ('my lovingkindness', as in the KJV's 'the God of my mercy'). The verse's only note (alternative_rendering, on 'mine enemies') concerns English wording elsewhere and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 59:15 'They shall wander up and down for food' is an intransitive rendering that fits both the qere hiphil יְנִיע֣וּן and the ketiv qal ינועון; no italicized supply or mapped textual note distinguishes them, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
